task.name: UI click detection breaks for the control with GameObject id 1
task.prompt: UiSystem::Interact uses the literal GameObjectId{1} as a sentinel meaning "the primary button press began over empty space". When the top-most / first clickable UI control actually has id 1 (e.g. a Button created as the only object in a fresh ObjectStore), a press+release over it is discarded as an empty-space press, so no click / clicked signal is produced. Reproduce: create one GameObject2D with a Button behavior, Build, Interact(press) then Interact(release) over it - expect one click, get none.
task.requirements: Interact reports a click for a press+release over a control regardless of its GameObjectId; the empty-space case still produces no click.
task.notes: UiSystem::Interact tracked an in-progress primary press with pressedOn_ and overloaded the literal GameObjectId{1} as a "began over empty space" sentinel, so a control whose real id was 1 could never register a click. Replaced the magic value with an explicit bool pressActive_; pressedOn_ now holds 0 for the empty-space case. Found while building ZE-66 (a Button that is the only object in a store gets id 1). Covered by the new UiTests ButtonStatesAndSignals case. Full ctest 35/35.

task.name: UI runtime + scripting - make the UI fully interactive and script-driven
task.prompt:
The UI subsystem (ZE-61/66/81/95) can be authored in the editor and rendered, but it is not yet a usable interactive UI at runtime. Close every runtime gap so a real game menu / HUD can be built entirely from scripts and the editor, with nothing left for 1.0 except bug fixes and small tweaks.
Current state to build on: - ui:: control classes exist (17 types), the GameObject2D tree is the UI tree, UiSystem lays out + batches + hit-tests + does press/release/click + TextEntry focus/typing at the engine level, and UiControl/UiSerialize expose every property. Scripts get native classes (uiControl..uiHtml) with clicked / pressed / released signals that DO dispatch to handlers in a running game. - The hard gap: ScriptHost::Synchronize / Invoke write-back is 3D-only (`As3D(native); if(!g) return;` at src/ScriptHost.cpp ~251 and the write-back loop ~270-279). A script attached to a UI control can LISTEN but cannot READ OR WRITE its own control's fields at runtime - `size = Vector2(...)`, `anchor = "center"`, `text = "Hi"`, `value = 0.5`, `visible = false`, `color = ...` etc. are all silently dropped. Transform2D position/rotation/scale is not synced either. - PlayerMain never pumps WM_CHAR into ui.Interact(..., typed), so TextEntry cannot be typed into in a built game. The editor Play preview does not route UI pointer or keyboard input at all. - Button and UiHtml only fire a bare "clicked" - a script cannot tell WHICH button or link inside an html block was activated.
What "done" means: build a scripted, interactive menu (buttons that change state, a text field you can type into, a value the script drives, a panel the script shows/hides) that works both in the editor Play preview and in a standalone build, using only scripts + the scene tree.
task.requirements: A script class that inherits a ui:: type (e.g. class Menu : uiPanel) can read and write EVERY serialized property of its control at runtime (base: anchor, size, min_size, order, visible, clickable; and every per-type field - text, value, color/tint, texture names, padding, spacing, fill_cross, scroll_x/y, horizontal, playing, loop, speed, html, background, margins, slice, pixel_height, placeholder, region, vertical, fill_color, background_color, disabled, per-state button colours/textures). Transform2D position/rotation/scale on a 2D object round-trips through the script proxy like the 3D Transform does. TextEntry can be typed into (keyboard) and queried both in the editor Play preview and in a standalone build; Enter fires a `submitted` signal. Button / UiHtml report which element was activated (a script can identify the clicked button or link). Hover and focus signals (mouse_entered, mouse_exited, focus_entered, focus_exited) fire on controls. Tab / Shift-Tab move focus between focusable controls; Enter / Space activate the focused button; Esc blurs. A control (or panel subtree) under the pointer consumes the click so it does NOT also reach the 3D game input / raycast layer, and the game can query "did the UI take the pointer / keyboard this frame". The editor Play preview routes UI pointer + wheel + keyboard so UI can be tested without a build. Scripts can build and change the UI tree at runtime: get parent / children, find a descendant by name, add / remove / reparent ui controls, spawn a UI prefab and get its root. Full ctest green; editor + player build; the demo menu described in the prompt works end to end.

task.name: UI visuals + assets - real images, text layout, scaling, video, so nothing UI is left for 1.0
task.prompt: Finish the UI's visual + asset side using the texture/material infrastructure from ZE-64/65. After this task the UI system is considered feature-complete for 1.0 - only bug fixes and minor tweaks after here. Current gaps: - Images do not load. TextureRect, PanelContainer texture, Button per-state textures and inside UiHtml all resolve to the 1x1 white texture (UiContext::resolveTexture returns renderer.WhiteTexture()). Nine-slice therefore has nothing real to sample. - Inspector texture fields (texture, normal/hover/pressed_texture, html src) are plain text boxes - no asset picker, no drag-drop of an image asset onto the field. - Text controls are top-left only: no horizontal / vertical alignment, and LongText honours explicit newlines but does not word-wrap to its box width. A real HUD needs wrapped, aligned text. - No UI scaling: layout is in raw window pixels, so a UI authored at one window size looks wrong at another. Need a design/reference resolution + scale mode (keep aspect / stretch / fixed) so authored UI is resolution-independent. - Disabled state does not propagate: disabling a container/panel does not disable its children for input or dim them. - VideoTexture shows a white rect in the editor (no resolveVideoFrame wired in EditorShell) and there is no way to create a .zvid asset from the editor (VideoClip::Encode exists but is not exposed), so video is not usable end to end. - Confirm real font-atlas text rendering works for every text-bearing control at the final scale.
task.requirements: TextureRect, PanelContainer, Button (all states) and UiHtml display real image files (png/jpg/bmp/tga/... from the asset library) via the renderer texture path; nine-slice samples the real texture correctly. The Inspector exposes a proper asset picker for every texture field (browse + drag an image asset from the library onto the field), and the field stores the project-relative asset path. Text and LongText support horizontal (left/center/right) and vertical (top/middle/bottom) alignment, and a word-wrap mode that wraps to the control's width; UiHtml lays out wrapped paragraphs. A UI reference/design resolution + scale mode (keep-aspect / stretch / fixed) makes authored UI look correct at any window size, in the editor and in a build. Disabling a container or panel disables input for and visually dims its whole subtree. VideoTexture previews real frames in the editor viewport, and a .zvid asset can be created from the editor (e.g. right-click -> build .zvid from an image-sequence folder, or import); the player already plays it. All text-bearing controls render through the real font atlas at the active scale. Full ctest green; editor + player + a RELEASE build (zip the release build for GitHub); a visual QA capture of a populated UI.

task.name: drag cursor feedback - show a valid / invalid drop cursor while dragging
task.prompt:
When the user is mid-drag in the editor (dragging a scene-tree object, an asset from the library, a prefab, etc.) the mouse cursor should tell them whether the thing under the pointer will accept the drop.
- While a drag is in progress and the pointer is over a target that WILL accept what is being dragged (the right reference type for an Inspector field, a valid reparent target in the scene tree, a valid folder in the library, the viewport for a prefab, etc.), change the cursor to a "this is a valid drop" cursor (e.g. IDC_CROSS or a copy/link cursor - pick one and use it consistently). - While dragging over anything that will NOT accept the drop (empty space, a wrong-type field, an illegal reparent), show the standard "no drop" cursor (IDC_NO). - The moment the pointer leaves a valid target (dragged back off), the cursor returns to the not-valid state; leaving the drag entirely / dropping / cancelling restores the normal arrow. - This is purely a cursor/feedback change - it must not alter what drops are actually accepted or how they behave.
Covers every existing editor drag source and drop target (scene-tree -> Inspector reference fields, scene-tree reparent, scene-tree -> viewport prefab spawn, asset library rows -> folders, asset -> Inspector, prefab/model drops). Route it through one shared "what would happen if I dropped here" hit-test so new drag types get the feedback for free.
task.requirements: During any editor drag, the cursor shows a distinct "valid drop" shape over targets that would accept the current payload and a "no drop" shape everywhere else, updates immediately as the pointer moves between targets (including dragging back off a valid target), and reverts to the normal cursor when the drag ends, drops, or is cancelled. Drop acceptance and behaviour are unchanged. There is a single reusable predicate the cursor logic and the actual drop handlers both consult, so it stays correct as drag types are added.

Wired for every current drag source/target: scene-tree -> Inspector reference field, scene-tree reparent, scene-tree -> viewport prefab, library row -> folder, asset -> Inspector, prefab/model drop
Tests: the predicate returns the right accept/reject per (payload, target), and drop behaviour is unchanged

task.notes: First half of the Material system: a ".shader" asset is plain HLSL text. New src/ShaderAssets.{h,cpp} (in zEngineScriptTools, links d3dcompiler): IsShader/Resolve/Load/Save/Create (atomic writes, project containment - mirrors ScriptAssets) with a template shader (cbuffer Parameters + Texture2D + PSMain). shaders::Parse(source) extracts the parameters - cbuffer scalars (float/float2/3/4, default read from a trailing "// default: ..." comment) and top-level Texture2D slots - and compiles the pixel entry (PSMain, ps_5_0) with D3DCompile to prove the HLSL is valid, returning {parameters, compiled, errors}. shaders::Analyze(wsource) is the editor tokeniser (HLSL keyword/type/preprocessor sets, bracket balance) and folds in the D3DCompile diagnostics as inline errors. Editor: assetLibrary::Kind::Shader (icon + "Material Shader" label); library right-click "Create Material Shader (.shader)"; double-click opens it in the inline ScriptEditor. ScriptEditor is now extension-aware (bool hlsl_): shader vs script Resolve/Load/Save, shaders::Analyze for highlighting/errors, and the zEngine-script compiler pass + autocomplete index are skipped for HLSL. It only defines code + parameters - nothing is applied to any object yet (that is ZE-65). Tests: ScriptEditorTests gains an HLSL block (create/round-trip, Parse params + compile ok, invalid HLSL reported, Analyze valid/invalid, .shader opened + saved through the editor). Full ctest 35/35; builds/debug + builds/test built.
